verdicts.rationale: Decode seeds the registry on the fresh BaseMessage before unmarshaling, and UnmarshalJSON explicitly rejects a missing registry. These are cooperating halves of the registry-bound wire decoder.

UnmarshalJSON calls Registry.Create with the wire type and rejects its nil result. Create documents precisely that consumer and returns the registered payload factory result, establishing one payload-resolution responsibility.

schemaProvider explicitly mirrors Payload.Schema, and registration validation asserts this interface to compare the produced payload schema with its registration. The two contracts must agree for that check to operate.

MarshalJSON writes metadata timestamps in Unix milliseconds, while wireMillis reads that representation and preserves its zero-time convention. They define the encoding and decoding of the same metadata fields without a containment relationship.
WithTime directly replaces default metadata by calling NewDefaultMeta with the requested creation time and preserved source. The constructor determines the received-time behavior of this option.

Storable exposes facts through Triples() []Triple, and Triple defines those facts and their provenance fields. The interface and returned element contract are useful together when implementing or consuming entity facts.

AppendIdentityKey reads the six identity-bearing Triple fields and explicitly excludes the remaining timestamp, confidence, and expiry fields. The struct and key function jointly define graph-fact deduplication semantics.
canonicalObjectKey calls roundTripIsIdentity to decide whether normalization can be skipped. The predicate and its exclusion of numbers are integral to the persisted-object identity algorithm.

RuleFields is explicitly documented as implementing RuleReadable and returns the generic payload's declared Data projection. This concrete behavior supplies evidence for the interface's rule-access contract.

IndexingProfiler documents falling through to the registered floor when its hint is absent, while IndexingProfileFor returns that per-type floor. They describe complementary channels of the same indexing-profile policy, even though the consuming ingest path is not ported here.

BaseMessage.Validate directly calls m.payload.Validate(), which for GenericJSONPayload executes the second entity. They split one message-validation workflow into envelope and payload checks, so the evidence establishes useful co-inspection rather than harmful conflation.

Meta tracks message origin and lifecycle, whereas Triple records the source and assertion time of an individual graph fact. Shared provenance and timestamp vocabulary does not make these interchangeable responsibilities.

Keyable denotes dotted semantic addresses, while AppendIdentityKey produces an injective length-prefixed deduplication identity. The cited comments distinguish routing/storage addressing from suppressing repeated fact assertions.

shapeCheck.check accepts JSON-shaped input for payload serialization; roundTripIsIdentity identifies values safe to skip persistence normalization. Their similar type switches answer different questions, particularly for numeric values.

Type identifies message schemas by domain/category/version, and EntityType classifies graph entities by domain/type. The package documentation explicitly separates these similarly named dotted identifiers.

IndexingProfiler declares indexing policy, whereas ContentStorable locates and exposes stored text for extraction. Embedding and content terminology overlaps, but the interfaces represent policy selection and content access respectively.

RuleReadable exposes fields available to rules; Registry.Contracts returns mutation projection contracts containing birth predicates and predicate groups. The shared word projection refers to different consumers and contracts.

Registry.Build constructs a payload from workflow field mappings, while Decode reconstructs the complete wire-message envelope with registry-bound decoding. Their use of factories and JSON does not equate their input contracts or responsibilities.

writeIdentityField creates collision-resistant identity encoding; member formats readable paths for JSON-shape diagnostics. Their string-building and awkward-character handling serve deduplication and error reporting separately.

IsExpired tests graph-fact expiry, whereas NewDefaultMeta stamps message receipt metadata. The clock calls are superficial likeness, and the source explicitly keeps triple TTL separate from lifecycle timestamps.
